label: Photon Counting
blurb: Shows the shot the way it arrives in very dim light: one photon at a time. Light is not a smooth flow but a rain of separate packets, and each pixel catches a random whole number of them drawn from the Poisson statistics real detectors follow. At a fraction of a photon per pixel the picture is a scatter of single bright specks in the dark; as Photons rises the specks crowd together and the picture condenses out of them until, at a few hundred, it is back to normal. Every frame catches a fresh set. Photon size turns each catch into a soft splash as in an intensified or single photon camera, Monochrome counts like a detector without a colour filter, and dark counts add the stray thermal hits every sensor has. Keyframe Photons for a shot that gathers itself out of darkness.
